propositions: A code-reading gate does not warn when its running binary is behind the base ref it pins, allowing stale code to silently review current material.
When a gate's binary predates a config schema change in the base ref, unknown config keys are silently ignored instead of flagged as potential drift.
The gate must emit a non-fatal advisory warning when drift is detected (running build is strict ancestor of pinned sha), including build sha, build date, pinned sha, and commit count.
The drift warning must be emitted at most once per (build sha, pinned sha) pair per process to avoid duplication.
Config unknown-key messages should indicate potential build drift ('this build may predate it') when drift is detected, versus the default 'typo?' wording when no drift exists.
